questions.question: A product reaches a buyer from the farmer through 3 middlemen with the intermediate profits of 10%, 20% and 30%, respectively. Finally, the seller keeps a profit of 15%. If the farmer has sold the product at Rs. X, then how much more percent did the buyer pay for it?
questions.solution:
Given,

The successive profit of 3 middlemen = 10%, 20%, 30%

Let the cost price of product 100 Rs.

First middlemen sell this product on 10% profit

⇒ 100 × 110/100 = 110

Second middlemen sell this product on 20% profit

⇒ 110 × 120/100 = 132

Third middlemen sell this product on 30% profit

⇒ 132 × 130/100 = 171.6

According to question seller sell at 15% profit

⇒ 171.6 × 115/100 = 197.34

⇒ Required increased percentage = [(197.34 – 100)/100] × 100 = 97.34 %

questions.question: What are the organisms that eat other organisms called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holotrophic organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Holotrophic organisms** are those organisms that obtain their nutrition by **ingesting or consuming other organisms** or organic matter.
 
• This mode of nutrition is known as **holozoic nutrition**, where food is **ingested, digested, absorbed, and assimilated**.
 
• Examples include **humans, animals, amoeba**, and many other organisms that depend on other living organisms for food.
 
• **Statement-wise Analysis:**
 
 
• **Holotrophic organisms** – Feed by eating other organisms. **Correct**.
 
• **Parasitic organisms** – Live on or inside a host and derive nutrition, but not by directly ingesting whole organisms. **Incorrect**.
 
• **Chemotrophic organisms** – Obtain energy from chemical reactions, not by consuming organisms. **Incorrect**.
 
• **Saprotrophic organisms** – Feed on dead and decaying organic matter. **Incorrect**.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Holotrophic organisms.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Autotrophic Nutrition:** Organisms like **plants** prepare their own food using **photosynthesis**.
 
• **Heterotrophic Nutrition:** Organisms depend on others for food; includes **holozoic, parasitic, and saprophytic** types.
 
• **Parasitic Mode:** Example: **tapeworm**, which derives nutrients from a host organism.
 
• **Saprotrophic Mode:** Example: **fungi**, which decompose dead organic matter.
 
• **Chemotrophs:** Common in **bacteria** that obtain energy from oxidation of chemicals like **nitrogen or sulfur compounds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Holozoic Process Steps:** **Ingestion → Digestion → Absorption → Assimilation → Egestion**.
 
• This type of nutrition is mainly found in **higher organisms** including most animals.

questions.question: The potential energy (P.E) of a body at a certain height is 200 J. The kinetic energy possessed by it when it just touches the surface of the earth is (Neglect any air friction):
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

__
 
• **Law of the Conservation of energy: "**Energy can neither be created nor be destroyed. It just gets transfers in one form to another*.*"
 
• **Total energy (TE)**: The sum of the potential energy (PE) and kinetic energy (KE) is called total energy.

TE = KE + PE 

 
• **Potential Energy: T**he stored energy of a body by the virtue of its position is called potential energy.

 
 
• Example: A rock sitting at the edge of a cliff has potential energy.
 
 

PE = m g h 

Where m is mass, g is the acceleration due to gravity and h is the height 

 
• **Kinetic Energy:** The energy possessed by the body by virtue of being in motion is called kinetic energy.

KE = 1/2 m V² where V is the velocity of the body.

 
• Example: A ball thrown would have kinetic energy.

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• According to the** energy conservation principle**, the **sum of the kinetic energy and potential energy of the body always remains constant**. 
 
• As the **body comes down** the height of the body decreases and hence the **potential energy decreases**. If the potential energy decreases the **kinetic energy will increase**.
 
• As soon as the **body touches the ground**, **all the initial potential energy of the particle gets converted into kinetic energy**.
 
• The potential energy (P.E) of a body at a certain height is 200 J. The kinetic energy possessed by it when it just touches the surface of the earth is the same as the Potential Energy (= P.E.). **So the option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: What is ‘amu’ in the context of atoms and molecules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e __**Atomic Mass Unit.**__

__
 
• **Atomic Mass Unit**__ is the full form of "amu".
 
• **One Atomic Mass Unit:** It is defined as the mass equal to **one-twelfth** the mass of one** carbon- 12 **atom.
 
• And 1 amu = 1.66056 × 10⁻²⁴ g

Mass of an atom of hydrogen = 1.6736 × 10⁻²⁴ g

Thus, in terms of amu, the mass of hydrogen atom = (1.6736 × 10⁻²⁴) / (1.66056 × 10⁻²⁴) = 1.0078 amu

questions.question: Bleaching powder is produced by the action of chlorine on dry slaked lime. Which of the following is appropriate equation for this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e **Ca (OH)₂ + CI₂ = CaOCI₂ + H₂O**

__
 
• The **Chlorine** which is produced on passing electricity through brine solution further reacts with** slaked lime [Ca(OH)₂]** to produce bleaching powder.
 
• The reaction is as given below:

 **Ca (OH)₂ + CI₂ = CaOCI₂ + H₂O**

 
• Bleaching powder is also known as **Calcium Oxychloride (CaOCl₂).**__

 

​**Uses of Bleaching powder:**

 
• It is used to bleach washed clothes in the industry.
 
• Used as a disinfectant.
 
• Used as an oxidizing agent in many chemical industries.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right provided in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e __**Right to Property**__

__
 
• **Right to Property**__ is not a **Fundamental Right** provided in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Right to Property** was removed from the Fundamental Rights in **1978** under the** 44th Constitutional Amendment** **Act** and it was placed in the new **Article 300A **as an ordinary** legal right**.

questions.question:
We all know from our observation that water can exist in three states of matter.

Statements:

A. Solid, as ice

B. Liquid, as petrol and

C. Gas as O₂

Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.text: Only A is true, B and C are false
A and B are true, C is false

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A is true, B and C are false.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Water can exist in three states of matter as **solid, liquid,** and **gas.**

**Solid water:__** 

__
 
• When water freezes, its molecules move farther apart, making **ice** less dense than water.
 
• Hence, ice is lighter than the same volume of water, and so ice will float in water. Water freezes at **0°C, 32° F.**
 
• **Ice, snow, and frost** are examples of water in the solid-state. Liquid water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius. 
 
• Celsius is a scale that measures temperature.
 
• It is possible to solidify water without allowing it to crystallize.
 
• This has been demonstrated in laboratory conditions decades ago, using metal plates chilled with dry ice or liquid nitrogen and slamming them together to trap a falling water drop between.

**Liquid water:__** 

__
 
• It is the most familiar form of water which we use in drinking, bathing, washing clothes, etc.
 
• **Clouds, snow, and rain** are all made up of some form of water. A cloud is comprised of tiny water droplets and/or ice crystals, a snowflake is an aggregate of many ice crystals, and rain is just liquid water.
 
• The equation for the formation of liquid water is: **2H2(g)+O2(g)→2H2O(l) 2 H 2 ( g ) + O 2 ( g ) → 2 H 2 O ( l )** .

**Gaseous water:__**

 
• Water vapors and steam are the gaseous forms of liquid.
 
• Steam is formed at **100°C, 212°F.**
 
• Water existing as gas is called **water vapor**.
 
• When referring to the amount of moisture in the air, we are actually referring to the amount of water vapor.

questions.question: There are ________ parallel ranges of the Himalayas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e __**Three**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

The **three** parallel ranges of Himalayas are:

**__Himadri (Great or Inner Himalayas)__**

__
 
• It is the most continuous range with an average height of **6000** meters.
 
• It remains covered with snow throughout the year.

 

**Himachal (Lesser Himalayas)**__ 

__
 
• It lies to the south of Himadri.
 
• The average height of these mountains is between **3,700 to 4,500 meters.**
 
• Famous ranges are: **Pir Panjal range, Dhaula Dhar and Mahabharat ranges**.
 
• Famous valleys like** Kangra, Kullu, and Kashmir** are situated in this valley.

 

​**Shivalik (Outer Himalayas)**__

 
• These are outermost ranges of Himalayas and have an average height between** 900 to 1100** meters. 
 
• These ranges are mainly composed of unconsolidated rock material, so these ranges are prone to earthquakes and landslides.
 
• The longitudinal valleys lying between lesser Himalayas and Shiwaliks are called **‘Duns’** like** Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun, and Patlin Dun,** etc.
